    • Time step: \(\Delta t = 0.5\text{ hour}\)
    • Rainfall intensities from hyetograph:
      Interval (hr)Intensity (mm/hr)
      0.0 – 0.512.0
      0.5 – 1.04.5
      1.0 – 1.515.0
      1.5 – 2.014.0
      2.0 – 2.54.0
      2.5 – 3.07.5
      3.0 – 3.53.0
  • Aim: Determine the \(\phi\)-index (in mm/hour) for the given rainfall event.

3. Core Concepts:

Infiltration (\(F\)): Total water absorbed by the soil.\[F = P - R \]

W-index: Average infiltration rate over the entire storm duration (\(t\)).\[W_{index} = \dfrac{F}{t} \]

\(\phi\)-index: The constant rate of abstraction during the period of rainfall excess. Rainfall intensities less than \(\phi\) do not produce runoff and entirely infiltrate. The \(\phi\)-index satisfies \(\phi \ge W_{index}\).

Runoff Equation:\[R = \sum_{i=1}^{n}(I_i - \phi)\cdot\Delta t \quad \text{for all intervals where } I_i > \phi \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate total infiltration (\(F\)) and storm duration (\(t\)).
  2. Calculate the W-index to establish a lower bound for \(\phi\).
  3. Identify runoff-producing intervals by trial, excluding those where \(I_i < \phi\).
  4. Solve for \(\phi\) and verify the assumption.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total Infiltration and Duration:\[F = 30 - 16 = 14\text{ mm}, \quad t = 3.5\text{ hours} \]
  2. Lower Bound (W-index):\[W_{index} = \dfrac{14}{3.5} = 4\text{ mm/hr} \implies \phi \ge 4\text{ mm/hr} \]
  3. Trial for \(\phi\)-index:
    Since \(\phi \ge 4\text{ mm/hr}\), intensities \(I_5 = 4\text{ mm/hr}\) and \(I_7 = 3\text{ mm/hr}\) will not produce runoff.
    Assume \(\phi\) lies between \(4\text{ mm/hr}\) and \(4.5\text{ mm/hr}\). Runoff-producing intervals: \(I_1 = 12\), \(I_2 = 4.5\), \(I_3 = 15\), \(I_4 = 14\), \(I_6 = 7.5\).
  4. Solve for \(\phi\):\[ 16 = \left[(12-\phi)+(4.5-\phi)+(15-\phi)+(14-\phi)+(7.5-\phi)\right] \times 0.5 \]\[32 = 53 - 5\phi \implies 5\phi = 21 \implies \phi = 4.2\text{ mm/hr} \]
  5. Verification:
    Is \(4.2 < 4.5\)? ✓ Are discarded intensities (4 and 3) less than 4.2? ✓ Assumption is correct.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.2 mm/hour | Accepted key range: 4.2 to 4.2

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A venturimeter as shown in the figure (not to scale) is connected to measure the flow of water in a vertical pipe of 20 cm diameter.



Assume \( g = 9.8 \) m/s². When the deflection in the mercury manometer is 15 cm, the flow rate (in lps, round off to two decimal places) considering no loss in the venturimeter is ______________
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Fluid Dynamics & Flow Measurement

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Pipe (inlet) diameter: \(D_1 = 20\text{ cm} = 0.2\text{ m}\)
    • Throat diameter: \(D_2 = 10\text{ cm} = 0.1\text{ m}\)
    • Manometer fluid: Mercury (\(S_m = 13.6\))
    • Flowing fluid: Water (\(S_w = 1.0\))
    • Manometer deflection: \(x = 15\text{ cm} = 0.15\text{ m}\)
    • \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\)
    • No loss \(\implies C_d = 1.0\)
  • Aim: Find the flow rate (discharge) in litres per second (lps), rounded to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Piezometric Head Difference (\(h\)): For a differential U-tube manometer, orientation does not affect the formula:\[h = x\left(\dfrac{S_m}{S_w} - 1\right) \]

Venturimeter Discharge Formula:\[Q = \dfrac{C_d \cdot A_1 \cdot A_2}{\sqrt{A_1^2 - A_2^2}}\sqrt{2gh} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate cross-sectional areas \(A_1\) and \(A_2\).
  2. Calculate piezometric head difference \(h\) in metres of water.
  3. Compute discharge \(Q\) in m³/s using the venturimeter equation.
  4. Convert to litres per second (lps).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Areas:\[A_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.2)^2 = 0.031416\text{ m}^2, \quad A_2 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.1)^2 = 0.007854\text{ m}^2 \]Shortcut: Since \(D_1 = 2D_2\), we have \(A_1 = 4A_2\), so \(\dfrac{A_1 A_2}{\sqrt{A_1^2 - A_2^2}} = \dfrac{4A_2}{\sqrt{15}}\).
  2. Piezometric Head (\(h\)):\[h = 0.15 \times (13.6 - 1) = 0.15 \times 12.6 = 1.89\text{ m of water} \]
  3. Discharge (\(Q\)):\[Q = 1.0 \times \dfrac{4 \times 0.007854}{\sqrt{15}} \times \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 1.89} \]\[Q = \dfrac{0.031416}{3.87298} \times \sqrt{37.044} = 0.008112 \times 6.0864 = 0.049370\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]
  4. Unit Conversion:\[Q = 0.049370 \times 1000 = 49.37\text{ lps} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 49.37 lps | Accepted key range: 49.0 to 50.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question: A reservoir with a live storage of 300 million cubic metre irrigates 40000 hectares (1 hectare = 10⁴ m²) of a crop with two fillings of the reservoir. If the base period of the crop is 120 days, the duty for this crop (in hectares per cumec, round off to integer) will then be ______________
questions.explanation:
Irrigation Engineering | Water Requirements of Crops

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Live storage of reservoir: \(300 \times 10^6\text{ m}^3\)
    • Number of reservoir fillings: \(2\)
    • Irrigable area (\(A\)): \(40{,}000\text{ hectares}\)
    • Base period of crop (\(B\)): \(120\text{ days}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the duty for this crop in hectares per cumec (rounded to nearest integer).

3. Core Concepts:

Delta (\(\Delta\)): Depth of water applied over the irrigated area.\[\Delta = \dfrac{V}{A} \]

Duty (\(D\)): Area of land (in hectares) that can be irrigated by a continuous flow of 1 cumec over the base period.\[D = \dfrac{8.64\,B}{\Delta} \quad (\Delta\text{ in metres, }B\text{ in days}) \]

Verification via Discharge Method:\[Q = \dfrac{V}{B \times 86400}, \quad D = \dfrac{A}{Q} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the total usable water volume from two reservoir fillings.
  2. Calculate depth of water applied (\(\Delta\)) by dividing total volume by irrigated area.
  3. Use the \(\Delta\text{-}D\text{-}B\) relation to compute duty \(D\).
  4. Round to the nearest integer.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total Available Water Volume (\(V\)):\[V = 2 \times 300 \times 10^6 = 600 \times 10^6\text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Irrigated Area in SI units:\[A = 40{,}000\text{ ha} = 40{,}000 \times 10^4\text{ m}^2 = 400 \times 10^6\text{ m}^2 \]
  3. Calculate Delta (\(\Delta\)):\[\Delta = \dfrac{600 \times 10^6}{400 \times 10^6} = 1.5\text{ m} \]
  4. Calculate Duty (\(D\)):\[D = \dfrac{8.64 \times 120}{1.5} = \dfrac{1036.8}{1.5} = 691.2\text{ ha/cumec} \]
  5. Rounding: \(691.2 \approx\) 691 ha/cumec.

Verification via Discharge Method: \(Q = \dfrac{600 \times 10^6}{120 \times 86400} = 57.87\text{ cumecs}\). Then \(D = \dfrac{40{,}000}{57.87} = 691.2\text{ ha/cumec}\). ✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 691 ha/cumec | Accepted key range: 689 to 693

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
An activated sludge process (ASP) is designed for secondary treatment of 7500 m³/day of municipal wastewater. After primary clarifier, the ultimate BOD of the influent, which enters into ASP reactor is 200 mg/L. Treated effluent after secondary clarifier is required to have an ultimate BOD of 20 mg/L. Mix liquor volatile suspended solids (MLVSS) concentration in the reactor and the underflow is maintained as 3000 mg/L and 12000 mg/L, respectively. The hydraulic retention time and mean cell residence time are 0.2 day and 10 days, respectively. A representative flow diagram of the ASP is shown below.



The underflow volume (in m³/day, round off to one decimal place) of sludge wastage is ______________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Treatment / Activated Sludge Process

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Flow rate: \(Q = 7500\text{ m}^3/\text{day}\)
    • Ultimate BOD of influent: \(S_0 = 200\text{ mg/L}\)
    • Ultimate BOD of effluent: \(S_e = 20\text{ mg/L}\)
    • MLVSS in reactor: \(X = 3000\text{ mg/L}\)
    • MLVSS in underflow: \(X_u = 12000\text{ mg/L}\)
    • Hydraulic Retention Time: \(\theta = 0.2\text{ day}\)
    • Mean Cell Residence Time (Sludge Age): \(\theta_c = 10\text{ days}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the volume of underflow sludge wastage \(Q_w\) (in m³/day).

3. Core Concepts:

Hydraulic Retention Time (\(\theta\)):\[\theta = \dfrac{V}{Q} \]

Mean Cell Residence Time (\(\theta_c\)):\[\theta_c = \dfrac{V \cdot X}{Q_w \cdot X_u + (Q - Q_w) \cdot X_e} \]

Standard Assumption: Unless specified, suspended solids escaping in the treated effluent (\(X_e\)) is assumed to be zero.

Note: The BOD values \(S_0\) and \(S_e\) are distractor data — they are not needed for this SRT-based calculation.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the volume of the ASP reactor (\(V\)) using \(Q\) and \(\theta\).
  2. Use the SRT formula to isolate and solve for wastage discharge rate \(Q_w\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Volume of Aeration Tank (\(V\)):\[V = Q \times \theta = 7500 \times 0.2 = 1500\text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Underflow Wastage Rate (\(Q_w\)):
    Assuming \(X_e = 0\), the SRT equation simplifies to:\[\theta_c = \dfrac{V \cdot X}{Q_w \cdot X_u} \implies Q_w = \dfrac{V \cdot X}{\theta_c \cdot X_u} \]\[Q_w = \dfrac{1500 \times 3000}{10 \times 12000} = \dfrac{4{,}500{,}000}{120{,}000} = 37.5\text{ m}^3/\text{day} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 37.5 m³/day | Accepted key range: 37.0 to 38.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A grit chamber of rectangular cross-section is to be designed to remove particles with diameter of 0.25 mm and specific gravity of 2.70. The terminal settling velocity of the particles is estimated as 2.5 cm/s. The chamber is having a width of 0.50 m and has to carry a peak wastewater flow of 9720 m³/d giving the depth of flow as 0.75 m. If a flow-through velocity of 0.3 m/s has to be maintained using a proportional weir at the outlet end of the chamber, the minimum length of the chamber (in m, in integer) to remove 0.25 mm particles completely is ______________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Treatment / Grit Chamber

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis & Application
  • Given Data:
    • Particle diameter: \(d = 0.25\text{ mm}\)
    • Specific gravity of particle: \(G = 2.70\)
    • Terminal settling velocity: \(v_s = 2.5\text{ cm/s}\)
    • Width of chamber: \(B = 0.50\text{ m}\)
    • Peak wastewater flow: \(Q = 9720\text{ m}^3/\text{day}\)
    • Depth of flow: \(H = 0.75\text{ m}\)
    • Flow-through velocity: \(v_f = 0.3\text{ m/s}\)
  • Aim: Determine the minimum length of the chamber (\(L\)) in integer meters to achieve 100% removal of the 0.25 mm particles.

3. Core Concepts:

Discrete Particle Settling (Type-1): For complete removal, the settling time (\(t_s\)) must equal the hydraulic detention time (\(t_d\)).

\[t_d = \dfrac{L}{v_f}, \quad t_s = \dfrac{H}{v_s} \]

Equating the two:\[L = \dfrac{H \cdot v_f}{v_s} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert all velocities to SI units (m/s).
  2. Perform a sanity check on flow-through velocity using \(Q = A \cdot v_f\).
  3. Calculate required length \(L\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Unit Conversions & Sanity Check:
    \(v_s = 2.5\text{ cm/s} = 0.025\text{ m/s}\)
    \[Q = \dfrac{9720}{24 \times 3600} = 0.1125\text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]\[A = B \times H = 0.50 \times 0.75 = 0.375\text{ m}^2 \]\[v_f = \dfrac{0.1125}{0.375} = 0.3\text{ m/s} \; ✓ \]
  2. Minimum Length Calculation:\[L = H \times \dfrac{v_f}{v_s} = 0.75 \times \dfrac{0.3}{0.025} = 0.75 \times 12 = 9\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 9 m | Accepted key range: 9 to 9

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: In an aggregate mix, the proportions of coarse aggregate, fine aggregate and mineral filler are 55%, 40% and 5%, respectively. The values of bulk specific gravity of the coarse aggregate, fine aggregate and mineral filler are 2.55, 2.65 and 2.70, respectively. The bulk specific gravity of the aggregate mix (round off to two decimal places) is ______________
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Pavement Materials / Aggregate Testing

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    ComponentWeight % (\(W_i\))Bulk Specific Gravity (\(G_i\))
    Coarse Aggregate552.55
    Fine Aggregate402.65
    Mineral Filler52.70
  • Aim: Compute the bulk specific gravity of the aggregate mix (\(G_{mix}\)), rounded to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Weighted Harmonic Mean of Specific Gravities: When combining materials by weight percentage, the theoretical bulk specific gravity of the mixture is:\[G_{mix} = \dfrac{W_{total}}{\sum\left(\dfrac{W_i}{G_i}\right)} = \dfrac{100}{\dfrac{W_1}{G_1} + \dfrac{W_2}{G_2} + \dfrac{W_3}{G_3}} \]This ensures that the volumes of individual components add up correctly.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Divide each weight percentage by its corresponding specific gravity.
  2. Sum the quotients (represents total relative volume).
  3. Divide total weight (100) by this sum.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Individual volume proportions (\(W_i/G_i\)):
    • Coarse Aggregate: \(55/2.55 = 21.5686\)
    • Fine Aggregate: \(40/2.65 = 15.0943\)
    • Mineral Filler: \(5/2.70 = 1.8519\)
  2. Total relative volume:\[\sum\left(\dfrac{W_i}{G_i}\right) = 21.5686 + 15.0943 + 1.8519 = 38.5148 \]
  3. Compute \(G_{mix}\):\[G_{mix} = \dfrac{100}{38.5148} = 2.5964 \approx 2.60 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.60 | Accepted key range: 2.58 to 2.61

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: The stopping sight distance (SSD) for a level highway is 140 m for the design speed of 90 km/h. The acceleration due to gravity and deceleration rate are 9.81 m/s² and 3.5 m/s², respectively. The perception/reaction time (in s, round off to two decimal places) used in the SSD calculation is ______________
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Geometric Design / Stopping Sight Distance

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Stopping Sight Distance: \(SSD = 140\text{ m}\)
    • Design Speed: \(V = 90\text{ km/h}\)
    • Acceleration due to gravity: \(g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2\)
    • Deceleration rate: \(a = 3.5\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Find the perception/reaction time (\(t_r\)) in seconds used in this SSD calculation.

3. Core Concepts:

Stopping Sight Distance (SSD): Based on IRC specifications, SSD is the sum of the lag distance and braking distance:\[SSD = d_{lag} + d_{braking} = (v \cdot t_r) + \dfrac{v^2}{2a} \]where \(v\) is speed in m/s, \(t_r\) is perception/reaction time (s), and \(a\) is deceleration (m/s²).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert design speed from km/h to m/s.
  2. Calculate braking distance using the given deceleration rate.
  3. Subtract braking distance from total SSD to get lag distance.
  4. Divide lag distance by speed to find \(t_r\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert Design Speed:\[v = 90 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 25\text{ m/s} \]
  2. Braking Distance:\[d_{braking} = \dfrac{v^2}{2a} = \dfrac{(25)^2}{2 \times 3.5} = \dfrac{625}{7.0} = 89.286\text{ m} \]
  3. Lag Distance and \(t_r\):\[d_{lag} = SSD - d_{braking} = 140 - 89.286 = 50.714\text{ m} \]\[t_r = \dfrac{d_{lag}}{v} = \dfrac{50.714}{25} = 2.029\text{ s} \approx 2.03\text{ s} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.03 s | Accepted key range: 1.90 to 2.10

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: For a 2° curve on a high speed Broad Gauge (BG) rail section, the maximum sanctioned speed is 100 km/h and the equilibrium speed is 80 km/h. Consider dynamic gauge of BG rail as 1750 mm. The degree of curve is defined as the angle subtended at its center by a 30.5 m arc. The cant deficiency for the curve (in mm, round off to integer) is ______________
questions.explanation:
Railway Engineering | Geometric Design / Superelevation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Degree of Curve: \(D = 2^\circ\)
    • Arc length defining degree: \(L_{arc} = 30.5\text{ m}\)
    • Maximum sanctioned speed: \(V_{max} = 100\text{ km/h}\)
    • Equilibrium speed: \(V_{eq} = 80\text{ km/h}\)
    • Dynamic gauge (c/c rail distance): \(G = 1750\text{ mm} = 1.75\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the cant deficiency (\(C_d\)) in mm (rounded to nearest integer).

3. Core Concepts:

Radius of Curve (\(R\)):\[R = \dfrac{L_{arc} \times 180}{\pi \times D} \]

Theoretical Cant (\(e\)):\[e = \dfrac{G \cdot V^2}{g \cdot R} \quad (V\text{ in m/s}) \quad \text{or} \quad e = \dfrac{G \cdot V^2}{127R} \quad (V\text{ in km/h}) \]

Cant Deficiency (\(C_d\)): Shortfall in cant when a train travels at \(V_{max}\) while actual cant was designed for \(V_{eq}\).\[C_d = e_{th\,(V_{max})} - e_{actual\,(V_{eq})} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Evaluate radius \(R\) from the arc definition.
  2. Calculate actual cant (\(e_{actual}\)) provided for equilibrium speed.
  3. Calculate theoretical cant required (\(e_{th}\)) for maximum speed.
  4. Subtract to find cant deficiency and convert to mm.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Curve Radius (\(R\)):\[R = \dfrac{30.5 \times 180}{\pi \times 2} = \dfrac{2745}{\pi} \approx 873.76\text{ m} \]
  2. Actual Cant (\(e_{actual}\)) at \(V_{eq} = 80\text{ km/h} = 22.222\text{ m/s}\):\[e_{actual} = \dfrac{1.75 \times (22.222)^2}{9.81 \times 873.76} = \dfrac{1.75 \times 493.827}{8571.58} = 0.10082\text{ m} = 100.82\text{ mm} \]
  3. Theoretical Cant (\(e_{th}\)) at \(V_{max} = 100\text{ km/h} = 27.778\text{ m/s}\):\[e_{th} = \dfrac{1.75 \times (27.778)^2}{9.81 \times 873.76} = \dfrac{1.75 \times 771.605}{8571.58} = 0.15753\text{ m} = 157.53\text{ mm} \]
  4. Cant Deficiency (\(C_d\)):\[C_d = 157.53 - 100.82 = 56.71\text{ mm} \approx 57\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 57 mm | Accepted key range: 55 to 59
